title: Smooth pullback cohomology and support dimension
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth morphism of constant relative dimension $d$ between separated schemes of finite type over a field $k$, and let $K$ be a bounded constructible $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-coefficient complex on $Y$ in the categories of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. For every integer $i$, derived pullback is exact on the cohomology sheaves and there is a canonical identification $\mathcal H^{-i}(Lf^*K[d])\cong f^*\mathcal H^{-i+d}(K)$. Consequently, with supports and their dimensions as in [def-per-support-condition], $$\dim\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^{-i}(Lf^*K[d])\le \dim\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^{-i+d}(K)+d.$$

source.place: Stacks Tag 0AFF, Lemma \ref{lemma-smoothness-dimension} ($\dim_x(X)=\dim_y(Y)+\dim_x(X_y)$ for a smooth morphism of locally Noetherian schemes), applied to the base change of $f$ to the reduced support; the cohomology identification is the exactness of inverse image on cohomology sheaves

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres] in the coefficient categories specified in the statement. Its degree-zero pullback preserves short exact sequences: at a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$ the resulting sequence identifies with the original sequence at $f\bar x$, and the exact, jointly conservative geometric fibre functors detect exactness. Its exact triangulated functor $Lf^*$ therefore preserves both halves of the bounded standard t-structure. Explicitly, an object with cohomology in $[a,b]$ is built from its finitely many cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^j(K)[-j]$ by the ordinary truncation triangles; pullback takes each such term to a sheaf in the same degree. Induction on $b-a$, using that $D^{\le r}$ and $D^{\ge r}$ are closed under extensions and the long exact cohomology sequence of each distinguished triangle (clauses 2 and 5 of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles]), leaves the interval unchanged. Thus pullback of the canonical truncation triangle at any integer $r$ is again a truncation triangle: its first term has degrees at most $r$, and its last term has degrees at least $r+1$. Since a truncation triangle at $r$ is unique up to unique isomorphism and the truncations are functors (clause 1 of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles], for the t-structure of [def-weil-t-structure] specified in [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres]), this gives the canonical comparisons with the truncations of $Lf^*K$. Taking the degree-$r$ term gives the natural isomorphism $\mathcal H^r(Lf^*K)\cong f^*\mathcal H^r(K)$ of cohomology objects; by the cited adic lemma these are, at a finite stage, the images of the ambient cohomology sheaves of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] of integral representatives. All maps are at a common finite coefficient field and compatible with enlargement by the cited fibre lemma, so the identification is canonical in the specified $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ category.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; bounded truncation argument spelling out the first paragraph of the blueprint proof

proof.text: For the cohomological shift convention, a representative $C[d]$ has term $C^{n+d}$ in degree $n$ and differential $(-1)^d d_C^{n+d}$. Multiplication of a differential by $\pm1$ changes neither its kernel nor its image, so the quotient description of [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] gives $\mathcal H^n(C[d])\cong\mathcal H^{n+d}(C)$. Set $n=-i$ and use Step 1 with $r=-i+d$. This gives the asserted canonical identification $\mathcal H^{-i}(Lf^*K[d])\cong f^*\mathcal H^{-i+d}(K)$.

Put $\mathcal F=\mathcal H^{-i+d}(K)$, and let $S$ be its nonzero-geometric-fibre locus in $Y$. By [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres], this is constructible, independent of the chosen geometric point over a given point. The same lemma gives $(f^*\mathcal F)_{\bar x}\cong\mathcal F_{f\bar x}$, so this fibre is nonzero exactly when $f(x)\in S$. For an object of the $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-coefficient heart, the support in [def-per-support-condition] is read as this nonzero-geometric-fibre locus, which depends only on the isomorphism class: the support of the ambient cohomology sheaf of an integral representative can be enlarged by $\varpi$-power torsion that is zero in the rational category. Hence $\operatorname{Supp}(f^*\mathcal F)=f^{-1}S$. If supports are instead taken as closures of these loci, Step 6 shows that the dimensions are unchanged. If $S$ is empty, both support dimensions in the desired inequality are $-\infty$, with $-\infty+d=-\infty$, and the result follows. Assume henceforth that $S$ is nonempty.

source.place: Definitions 6.8.6 and 6.8.10 and Remark 6.8.15; the blueprint first-paragraph support-preimage calculation

proof.text: Let $Z$ be the reduced closed subscheme of $Y$ with underlying closed subset $\overline S$, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. By [lem-per-constructible-subset-closure-dimension], $\dim Z=\dim S$. Form $W=X\times_Y Z$ and its projection $g:W\to Z$. By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence], $g$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], $W\to X$ is a closed immersion and identifies its underlying space with $f^{-1}(\overline S)$. On affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $f$ where $Z$ is cut out by $I\subseteq R$, this identification is the equality $B\otimes_R(R/I)=B/IB$: a prime of $B$ lies in this closed subscheme exactly when its contraction contains $I$. Both $Z$ and $W$ are finite type over $k$: in affine finite-type charts of $Y$ and $X$ their closed subschemes are spectra of quotients of finitely generated $k$-algebras, and finite affine covers suffice. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], both are Noetherian, since a field has only the ideals $0$ and $k$ and hence is Noetherian. These are precisely the local Noetherian hypotheses needed below. No claim that $S$ itself is closed is used.

source.place: Tag 0AFF applied after smooth base change to the reduced closure of the constructible support

proof.text: For each $w\in W$ with $z=g(w)$, [lem-per-smooth-local-dimension] and the relative-dimension convention of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] give $\dim_w W=\dim_z Z+d$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions], $\dim_z Z\leq\dim Z$ and $\dim W=\sup_{w\in W}\dim_w W$. Taking this supremum yields $\dim W\leq\dim Z+d$. If $W$ is empty the same bound follows from $\dim W=-\infty$, so no surjectivity of $f$ onto the support is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0AFF, lemma-smoothness-dimension, and the supremum of local topological dimensions

proof.text:
For any subset $A$ of a topological space $B$, closing in $B$ each term of a chain of irreducible closed subsets of $A$ gives a chain of irreducible closed subsets of $B$ of the same length: closure preserves irreducibility, and intersecting those closures with $A$ recovers the original closed subsets, so strictness is preserved. Thus $\dim A\leq\dim B$. Apply this to $f^{-1}S\subseteq |W|$ with the induced topologies. Steps 2–5 now give
$$\dim\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^{-i}(Lf^*K[d])=\dim(f^{-1}S)\leq\dim W\leq\dim Z+d=\dim S+d=\dim\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^{-i+d}(K)+d.$$
This includes a pullback with empty support. If supports are taken as closures, the outer terms do not change: $\dim\overline S=\dim S$ by [lem-per-constructible-subset-closure-dimension] on $Y$; and $f^{-1}S$ is the union of the preimages of finitely many locally closed pieces of $S$, which are locally closed by continuity, so it is constructible in the Noetherian space $|X|$ by [def-weil-constructible-subset], and the same lemma on the finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ gives that its closure has dimension $\dim f^{-1}S$. This completes the inequality for every integer $i$.
